title: HTTP stop responding after some time
body:
Qdrant stops responding after some time with normal workload.

## Current Behavior
HTTP requests hangs forever

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Load data with upsert requests about 26 000 000 points
2. Start requesting via recommend endpoint (20 rps) while keep upserting new data (3 rps average)

Collection:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "status": "green",
    "optimizer_status": "ok",
    "vectors_count": 26434783,
    "indexed_vectors_count": 26423555,
    "points_count": 26434783,
    "segments_count": 13,
    "config": {
      "params": {
        "vectors": {
          "size": 312,
          "distance": "Cosine",
          "hnsw_config": {
            "m": 64,
            "ef_construct": 512,
            "on_disk": true
          },
          "quantization_config": {
            "scalar": {
              "type": "int8",
              "quantile": 0.99,
              "always_ram": false
            }
          },
          "on_disk": true
        },
        "shard_number": 1,
        "replication_factor": 1,
        "write_consistency_factor": 1,
        "on_disk_payload": true
      },
      "hnsw_config": {
        "m": 64,
        "ef_construct": 512,
        "full_scan_threshold": 10000,
        "max_indexing_threads": 0,
        "on_disk": true
      },
      "optimizer_config": {
        "deleted_threshold": 0.2,
        "vacuum_min_vector_number": 1000,
        "default_segment_number": 0,
        "max_segment_size": null,
        "memmap_threshold": null,
        "indexing_threshold": 20000,
        "flush_interval_sec": 5,
        "max_optimization_threads": 1
      },
      "wal_config": {
        "wal_capacity_mb": 32,
        "wal_segments_ahead": 0
      },
      "quantization_config": null
    },
    "payload_schema": {
      "a": {
        "data_type": "integer",
        "points": 26434783
      }
    }
  },
  "status": "ok",
  "time": 0.001014069
}
```

3
```
# telnet 10.0.245.6 6333
Trying 10.0.245.6...
Connected to 10.0.245.6.
Escape character is '^]'.
GET /collections
```

Hangs forever

## Expected Behavior
HTTP interface works as expected

## Possible Solution
Not known

## Context (Environment)
`
> lsb_release -a
No LSB modules are available.
Distributor ID: Debian
Description:    Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)
Release:        12
Codename:       bookworm
32Gb, NVMe SSD, Hetzner VM 16 ADM cores.
`
`
docker run -p 6333:6333 -v /var/qdrant_storage:/qdrant/storage -e QDRANT__LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG qdrant/qdrant
`

## Detailed Description
Fix this hang, please

> I can provide you with a dataset. It is 46Gb in size.

Yeah, if you could that would be fantastic.

I did create a similar collection (twice now) with [`bfb`](https://github.com/qdrant/bfb).

```bash
bfb -n 26000000 -d 312 --on-disk-payload --on-disk-hnsw --on-disk-vectors true --quantization scalar --quantization-in-ram false --timeout 30
```

I'm currently running a search/recommend load on it, but I don't see the number of open files growing. It caps at about 200 total.

> @participant2 I want to stress that increase in open files happens after server stops responding to HTTP requests.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I'm afraid I cannot reproduce the problem at this time. I've tried various configurations with various loads, and have run it over night. Having 26 million new/old points, with 1k upserted every second and 500 recommendation requests concurrently and the payload filter as you described.

With all of this I was unable to trigger the HTTP getting stuck issue. The number of open files never surpassed 320 and fluctuated a bit, which are normal numbers.

For your information, I ran this on a machine with 24 AMD cores, 32GB RAM, an NVMe drive and Ubuntu 23.04. That makes it somewhat similar to your configuration.

I wonder if we can greatly simplify the testing scenario to make debugging a lot easier.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant2 , Interesting observation. When I do recommend requests without any additional filters. Using only point id as a recommend parameter. The server stops hanging.
